notes:
PASS on the fake backend only: the gate prints evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level, and no hardware was attached. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review, and no ROS graph, Gazebo process, simulator run, rosbridge connection or hardware run is claimed. The upstream install command (pip install -r requirements.txt) was not run and no network was used.

SCOPE. The package serves the simulated Franka Hand gripper through the C++ PandaGripperController spawned by panda_sim_controllers.launch: the absolute action servers /franka_gripper/move (franka_gripper/MoveAction), /franka_gripper/grasp (franka_gripper/GraspAction) and /franka_gripper/stop (franka_gripper/StopAction), plus sensor_msgs/JointState on /franka_gripper/joint_states. Endpoints and generated types cite panda_sim_controllers/src/panda_gripper_controller.cpp:28-31 (the four action includes) and :38-58 (the SimpleActionServer registrations); the state publisher is cited at :163 and the two finger positions at :170-182. The action names are absolute in the constructor, so the declared root endpoints match the upstream strings.

The /franka_gripper/homing action is deliberately NOT bound: its handler only logs 'Homing not implemented for simulator.' and never calls setSucceeded or setAborted (panda_gripper_controller.cpp:269-271), so a caller would wait for a result that never arrives. The /franka_gripper/grasp handler performs the same width/speed position move as /move and does not read the goal force or epsilon fields (:292-325); the driver sends fixed zero values for those required goal fields and exposes no force input. The move and grasp callbacks loop on wall-clock time and measured width and do not check is_preempt_requested (:249-258, :313-321), so both actions are declared cancellable=false even though the actionlib servers exist.

NOT COVERED: the seven-joint arm trajectory action server, the /panda_simulator/motion_controller/arm/joint_commands topic, the arm robot_state/tip_state/joint_states topics and the MoveIt integration. This is a deliberate scope choice, not an observation-only replacement of motion: the gripper's primary move/grasp/stop action interface is fully served, and the pinned clone exposes no acknowledged arm stop service and no fixed arm stop action. The arm trajectory server's preempt callback calls franka_interface's exit_control_mode (:332-337), but the SDK does not accept action cancellation as a safety stop and cannot confirm quiescence, so a whole-arm driver would have to invent a stop path. The gripper is served because its upstream StopAction is a real, acknowledged stop of the simulated gripper. A future whole-arm package needs a source-backed stop endpoint, not an analytic stand-in.

SAFETY. The device is simulated at R2 (above the card's R1 floor). The fixed, input-free /franka_gripper/stop action is both the native e-stop binding and the declared safe-state action. Its handler sets the finger position command to the current measured finger positions, sets the speed command to zero, and answers success=true (panda_gripper_controller.cpp:273-288). The runtime latches before invoking it; after an e-stop, commands are refused with MHS.SAFETY.ESTOP_ENGAGED until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch. This is a native stop of the simulated gripper, not a physical emergency stop, and it does not control the arm. The fake's stop result is synthesized and does not prove physical quiescence.

LIMITS. The clone clamps the finger command to the URDF joint limits and the speed to the URDF velocity limit (panda_gripper_controller.cpp:231-236, :295-300) but states no numeric opening or speed bound in a text file; the 0.1 m/s default_speed and 0.005 m default_grasp_epsilon are configurable ROS parameters (panda_gazebo/config/robot_details.yaml:74-81) and the controller does not use them in the move/grasp handlers. Width and speed are therefore Limit.operator_required: eve [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the move, grasp and stop action bindings and the joint-state read against the pinned controller (absolute names, panda_gripper_controller.cpp:38-58; types 28-31; the configured pub_topic, panda_gripper_controller.yaml:4 and 153-164), the operator_required width and speed bounds (the finger limits live in a URDF outside the clone), every fact and the stop: the franka_gripper StopAction writes a hold of the measured opening with a zero speed target into the command buffers that update() applies through updateCommands() every fifth call to the finger effort PIDs with no mode branch (273-288, 187-225; panda_joint_position_controller.cpp:202-253), an acknowledged hold command, so the binding was kept. Defects: safe_state did not say that success is acknowledged before the controller applies the hold, that a move or grasp goal still running ignores the stop and cancellation for up to 5 s of ROS time (a reviewer probe with a goal that stays running showed the e-stop then fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held) or that any later goal replaces the hold; two facts said the waits loop on wall-clock time although they use ros::Time::now() (simulated time under the default use_sim_time of panda_world.launch) and ended in 'so ...' inferences; the default_speed fact claimed use outside its range; the joint-state binding and fact cited the unused else branch (163); the fake answered a cancel with PREEMPTED, which the pinned callbacks never produce; and the gripper_action_server_emulator that panda_world.launch starts by default, which re-commands the fingers at 20 Hz while its GripperCommand goal runs, was not disclosed. The reviewer rewrote safe_state, the docstring and the stop description, corrected ten facts and added eight (init start and timer, update and updateCommands, the finger PID, three launch defaults including use_sim_time, the emulator), widened the joint-state citation to 153-164 and added six fidelity gaps (driver.py); made the fake's cancel produce no terminal, added a hold_goals switch and an unstamped ROS 1 header (fake.py); added a case in which an e-stop during a running move fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held (test_driver.py); updated facts.md, also removing 'so a caller would wait forever' for homing; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged and the nine package cases pass; RESULT.json notes are stale where they say a homing caller waits for a result that never arrives, that the callbacks loop on wall-clock time and that test_driver.py adds eight cases. For the human reviewer: Simulated gripper only, but the endpoint names are those of franka_ros's real franka_gripper node (franka_ros is listed in dependencies.rosinstall, not in the clone): against a real Franka ROS graph these bindings would drive the real hand, including grasps with the fixed zero force and epsilon. The stop buffers a hold of the measured opening that the finger PIDs then keep; the acknowledgement precedes the hold and nothing senses that the fingers stopped. An e-stop during a running move or grasp stays unconfirmed (SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, latch held) until that goal ends after up to 5 s of simulated time, and never while Gazebo is paused. Any later move or grasp goal from another ROS client replaces the hold, including goals from the gripper_action_server_emulator that panda_world.launch starts by default (it re-commands the fingers at 20 Hz while a GripperCommand goal from MoveIt or another client runs). The action servers keep answering when a controller switch has stopped the gripper controller, and a stop is then acknowledged without effect. The Panda arm, the repository's main device, is NOT COVERED and has no acknowledged stop in the clone; an MHS e-stop does not stop it.
